what: static agreement audit of the weight-only refusal-axis constructions: pairwise cosines, norms, rank-1 shares, layer stability and subspace overlap, from safetensors bytes only

scope.why_static: a forward pass, a serve or a benchmark is out of scope; every number here is matrix algebra on published or committed weights

user_quant_stand_in.note: hashed only; every axis here comes from the float safetensors. Quantized-axis stability is not claimed by this card.

x1_twin_diff_svd.label: x1_twin_diff_svd
x1_twin_diff_svd.assumes: the published twin edit is rank-1 per writeback tensor (dW = -a r (W^T r)^T), so the top LEFT singular vector of twin-instruct is the residual direction that was removed; nothing about the axis is fitted and no token set is involved, the whole claim is the rank-1 shape.
x1_twin_diff_svd.space: residual stream (writeback output space), per layer

right_vector_cos_vs_Wtu.meaning: cos of the recovered right singular vector dW^T u/s1 with W_instruct^T u / ||W_instruct^T u||: 1.0 means the delta is exactly the rank-1 projection of the instruct writeback matrix along u, which is the abliteration construction

x1e_twin_embedding_delta.label: x1e_twin_embedding_delta
x1e_twin_embedding_delta.assumes: the twin edited model.embed_tokens.weight with the same rank-1 projection (dE = -(E r) r^T), so the RIGHT singular vector of the embedding delta is the residual direction r; this is a second, independent read of the twin axis from a different tensor shape.

x1b_twin_diff_column_norm.label: x1b_twin_diff_column_norm
x1b_twin_diff_column_norm.assumes: the removed residual direction is a COLUMN of dW (dW = -s u v^T), and the largest-norm column is that vector: no SVD and no rank assumption beyond rank-1. This is the heuristic the repo already uses in scripts/oracle_axis_alignment.py.
x1b_twin_diff_column_norm.space: residual stream (writeback output space), per layer

x3_alignment_delta_svd.label: x3_alignment_delta_svd
x3_alignment_delta_svd.assumes: the leading left singular vector of instruct-base is the "alignment direction"; the delta is high-rank and also carries instruction-following, so this construction assumes a refusal component lives on the leading axis.
x3_alignment_delta_svd.space: residual stream (writeback output space), per layer

x3b_alignment_column_norm.label: x3b_alignment_column_norm
x3b_alignment_column_norm.assumes: the removed residual direction is a COLUMN of dW (dW = -s u v^T), and the largest-norm column is that vector: no SVD and no rank assumption beyond rank-1. This is the heuristic the repo already uses in scripts/oracle_axis_alignment.py.
x3b_alignment_column_norm.space: residual stream (writeback output space), per layer

instruct.label: x4_head_geometry_instruct
instruct.assumes: the mean denial head row minus the mean compliance head row is the logit-space refusal direction and W_out^T (or E^T when tied) maps it to the residual direction that raises that margin; depends on the token sets, needs no activation and no forward pass.
instruct.logit_axis_note: u (151936-dim) is reproducible from the token ids and the head rows; only d is stored

base.label: x4_head_geometry_base
base.assumes: the mean denial head row minus the mean compliance head row is the logit-space refusal direction and W_out^T (or E^T when tied) maps it to the residual direction that raises that margin; depends on the token sets, needs no activation and no forward pass.
base.logit_axis_note: u (151936-dim) is reproducible from the token ids and the head rows; only d is stored

twin.assumes: the mean denial head row minus the mean compliance head row is the logit-space refusal direction and W_out^T (or E^T when tied) maps it to the residual direction that raises that margin; depends on the token sets, needs no activation and no forward pass.
twin.logit_axis_note: u (151936-dim) is reproducible from the token ids and the head rows; only d is stored

agreement.cos_matrix_note: SVD signs are arbitrary, so a matrix cell is |cos|; the signed value of each comparison is in global_signed and per_layer.

findings.reading: the twin delta is rank-1 per writeback tensor
the twin axis and the alignment axis target different residual subspaces
the twin embedding delta is rank-1 too
the embedding delta recovers the same residual direction as the writebacks: one direction across tensors of different shapes
the head-geometry axis is not the twin edit axis
the alignment axis is not the head-geometry axis
the twin axis is shared across layers and the alignment axis is layer-specific
the alignment delta is high-rank: its leading axis explains little of the delta energy
per-layer agreement is weaker than the global-vector agreement
x-4 is sensitive to the token set: the core-denial variant moves the axis
the affirmative-table compliance set moves x-4 almost completely: compliance-row choice is not a detail, it is half the construction
the twin delta is the rank-1 projection of the instruct writeback matrix along the recovered axis, to storage precision: the left vector alone is enough to reproduce the published edit shape
the alignment delta has no estimator-independent axis: the top singular vector and the largest-column heuristic disagree completely
fraction of the instruct writeback energy a rank-1 projection along the twin axis would remove
the twin edit is not confined to the writebacks: {'down_proj': 24, 'embed_tokens': 1, 'o_proj': 24}
the alignment delta touches every tensor, which is why its "axis" cannot be a single direction
